h1: What Every School Playground Should Include

props.title: What Every School Playground Should Include
props.summaryText: A checklist of what every school playground needs, from equipment for each kind of play to open space, safe surfaces, shade and supervision, with notes on why each one matters.
props.author: ananya-kulkarni
props.imageAlt: Installer working on new playground equipment at a school

takeaways.text: A good school playground offers every kind of play: climbing, sliding, swinging, spinning, balancing, pretending and running.
Separate zones for younger and older children prevent most collisions.
Open ground is as important as equipment: many games need space, not structures.
Safe surfaces, shade, water, seating and clear sight lines for staff complete the picture.

faq.q: What should a school playground have?
faq.a: Equipment for climbing, sliding, swinging, spinning and balancing; a separate zone for younger children; open ground for running games; impact-absorbing surfaces under equipment; shade, drinking water and seating; and a layout that staff can supervise from one point.

faq.q: How big should a school playground be?
faq.a: It depends on the number of children using it at the same time and their ages. Plan equipment so a whole break-time group can play without long queues, add safety zones around each unit, and keep open ground for running games. A supplier can propose a layout from your plot plan.

faq.q: What makes a school playground safe?
faq.a: Age-appropriate equipment designed to a recognised standard, impact-absorbing surfaces across all safety zones, a layout with clear routes and sight lines, simple rules, and regular inspection and maintenance.
